steps.report:
## Part 1 · What's working (Analyst)
Sources read in full: Legacy Posts (25 rows), Feedback & Lessons (all 200 rules), Batches, Posts (34), Post Performance (37), Conversion Windows, Formats, Visual Style, the assessment base (Submissions 19 rows, Visits 4 rows, non-personal fields only), and every file in `app/b4/`.

### Reach: three batches against her legacy
| | Legacy (25) | B1 (10) | B2 (12) | B3 (12) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Median views | **3,679** | ~450 | ~530 | ~510 |
| Posts over 1K | **24 of 25** | 2 | 4 | 2 |
| Slides | **4.3** | 7–9 | 7.8 | 7.6 |
| Words per line beat | **3.3** | n/a | 7.1 | 7.4 |
| Share of slides viewed | **48–63%** | ~30% | ~30–40% | 19–44% |

Small correction to the handoff: the legacy median is 3,679 (the 13th of 25), not ~3.4K.

**B3 day 1, ranked:** ملكة 1,729 · جمعة 1,008 · jacket 948 · nails 587 · biscuit 579 · hand dryer 552 · "no" 469 · checkout 450 · ride 442 · tower 416 · fast food 413 · losing game 378. Total ~7,970.

### The reusable pattern (legacy + B1–B3 agree)
1. **People in the scene who say something.** Every B3 post that got past the test audience had relatives talking (ملكة, جمعة, jacket). Public places with nobody reacting stalled 4 of 4 (checkout, ride, fast food, dryer). 4 of the 6 legacy breakouts have witnesses with lines (grandma's 203K, restaurant 39.5K, wall 16.8K, coffee shop 13.4K).
2. **The cost lands on her, in the first lines.** «والمشكله؟ أنت الطرف الخاسر» (159K), «فريق إنقاذ… لوحدك» (39.5K), and our own B1–B2 winners. Hooks that end on his behaviour stalled («وبدأ الصراخ», losing game, ride). «ما تقدري… إلا» is 0 of 4 and retired.
3. **Short beats and short posts.** Legacy says almost the same number of words in half the slides, at 3.3 words a beat with «…» pauses, and gets about twice the share of slides viewed. Ours read like instructions. Since slide-view share is a likely reach signal on TikTok photo posts, 7–8-slide posts are probably costing us distribution on their own.
4. **One tool that sounds like a trick, named and shown in action.** The wrong shoe, the last push, the traffic-light game. Sensible checklists got 1–2K.
5. **Humour that watches one detail, on her.** «صبرك طلع إجازة», the barista «كأنها شافت جريمة». Acting out the child's drama (bath, car seat) felt cringy and stalled at 3–6K.
6. **The ending surprises her.** The coffee-shop confession («بعد ١٢ جزمة… تقربي ترمي نفسك على الأرض معاه») is the model twist: a laugh at herself, not a reframe.
7. **Universal or strange-but-common moments beat narrow ones.** Leaving grandma's, the diaper, licking the wall. Narrow moments (drawers, the shouting post, outfits) got 0.9–3.9K even in her voice.

**Things that are not the driver:** format labels (F7 and F8 each went 1 of 3, and the winner was always the family scene), and A/B polls (they sit on winners and flops alike).

**The fade inside B3.** The first 6 posts averaged 878 views and the last 6 averaged 451, including the two posted alone on clean evenings. Weaker topics (home, no witnesses) plus one teal look 12 times in a row is the likeliest cause. That backs the visual refresh.

### Business (the funnel)
| | B1 | B2 | B3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Views (day 1, sum) | ~11.3K | ~14.3K | ~7.97K |
| Completed assessments | 0 | **9** | 2 |
| Views per completion | n/a | ~1.6K | **~4K** |
| Waitlist joins | 0 | 0 | 0 |

- **Completions follow reach plus a CTA that gets seen.** B1's reach posts had no CTA and got 0. B2 had both, and 5 of its 9 came within 19 hours of the hair-wash post. B3 had the CTA but little reach.
- **Emotions and outbursts lead, across all 19 completions ever:** Q14 = F for 8 (42%), sleep 5, communication 2, food 2, outings 1, other 1. Both B3 completions were F.
- **The leak after the assessment is the bigger business problem.** Of 19 mothers who completed, 8 clicked "learn more about the Living Plan", 2 clicked the waitlist button (both in October), and **0 have ever joined**. Since November, 6 Living Plan clicks led to 0 waitlist clicks. Content can't fix that alone. The odd-post QR codes (straight to the `?focus=` landing page) will show whether the landing route does better than the assessment route.
- **Comments:** 1 in all of B3. The one-word prompts («شيالة», «حارسة الباب») got 0. Only a question about her own child's preference has ever worked (wall post, 75 comments). Comments stay a minor signal (rule: zero comments isn't a failure).
- **Shares mark the posts people pass on:** "no" 4, ملكة/جمعة/jacket 3 each. In legacy, shares were the breakout marker (diaper 1,598, grandma's 1,106).

### Tracking check (Q12 / last_q)
- ✅ **last_q is fixed.** The Nov 24 completion (15:08 Saudi time) now reads **last_q = 15**. The handoff recorded 12.
- ✅ **A visit links to its submission.** That visit's session_id matches the Submissions id, so post tags will carry through from scan to completion.
- ✅ **The bio link is tagged.** Three visits on Nov 24 arrived with `src=bio`.
- ⚠️ **No partial start has ever been logged.** All 19 rows are `completed`, and only the newest has startedAt and last_q (the fields are new). Drop-off analysis only works if a mother who quits at Q5 still leaves a row with `status = started, last_q = 5`. **Please run one test:** open the assessment, answer about 5 questions, close the tab, and check that a row appears. Then delete it.
- ⚠️ **Three `src=bio` visits arrived within 17 seconds** (Nov 24, 18:18:50 → 18:19:07 Saudi time), each as a separate session, and none started the assessment. If that was you testing the new bio link, fine, and we can delete them. If it was one phone tapping the link three times, the "one per phone per session" dedupe isn't holding (TikTok's in-app browser may open a fresh session each tap), and visit counts per post will be inflated. Worth one check: tap the bio link twice from TikTok on one phone and see whether one or two rows appear.
- ℹ️ **No QR scans yet.** That's expected, since no B4 posts are live.

### Three instructions for this brief
1. **Every post opens on a moment with people reacting, with lines (or a universal or strange-but-common moment), and the cost on her.** At least 8 of 12.
2. **Write in her legacy voice, at legacy length:** 4–5 slides for one tool, 6 at most, and the tool on slide 3.
3. **Measure the post past the view:** a per-post QR code, the Visits and Submissions tags, and an alternating landing vs assessment route, so we finally learn which post sends mothers, and which route turns them into waitlist joins.

---

## Part 2 · Batch 4 brief (for you to confirm)
Built on the draft in `app/b4/step1_report.md`, with the Part 2b revisions and every Batch 4 decision in the handoff. Where the draft and the handoff differ, the handoff wins (4–5 / 6 slides, two posts a day, alternating QR routes).

**The job.** Breakouts that send mothers through a per-post QR code. Every post gives real value first, and the only ask is at the end. There's no attention vs conversion split.

**Audience.** A cold Saudi mother of a young child whose behaviour she's trying to handle. She doesn't know Home Orbit. We describe what she sees, never a diagnosis.

**Win, in order:**
1. Per-post QR visits, starts, completions, Living Plan clicks and waitlist joins (Visits and Submissions, by `post` tag).
2. Shares, saves, share of slides viewed.
3. Views. Comments count least.

**Size and cadence.** 12 static carousels over 6 evenings, two a day: one about 7:00 PM, the next 8:00–8:30 PM, never minutes apart.

### Voice (her legacy voice is the default)
- **Short beats** of 2–5 words, one idea a line, «…» pauses.
- **The opening:** a stamp («في المطعم…»), then the calm-vs-her turn («وأنتي؟»), then call-and-response («تحاولي… هو…»), then «وفجأة».
- **2–4 real quoted lines** from the people around her, plus her inner voice.
- **ONE comic image** casting HER in an adult role, at most one about the child, and never acted-out drama.
- **One love line** that clears her.
- **The tool** has a name in quotes and is shown working in 2–3 beats.
- **The ending** is a playful confession, then the CTA.
- **First person is allowed** («خليني أوريك», «قوليلي», «بيننا»). "We" parents stays banned.
- **Still banned:** «طبيعي», brain or nervous-system lines, emoji bullets, medical disclaimers, acting out his drama, homework endings, "follow for part 2".
- **Long sentences only in the final CTA** and in checklist items.
- **All 200 Feedback & Lessons rules still apply.** That covers her word list, «عشان» not «كذا», «خطوة», «يبكي», straight quotes for spoken lines, no line ending in a comma, and the realism checks.

### Structure (Part O)
- **One tool, 4–5 slides:** hook (pain + her cost) → deepen → **the tool on slide 3** → proof (our method described, never testimonials; it can carry the explainer) → twist + CTA + QR.
- **Three steps, 6 slides at most:** hook → deepen → steps → proof → twist + CTA + QR.
- **No ask before the last slide.** An optional "keep reading" line on 6-slide posts only, as a promise that asks nothing of her.

### Slate (12)
| Group | Count | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **«الافتراض اللي يصعّب الموضوع»** (her 200K format) | 4 | A new on-brand look, fewer words per slide, 5–6 slides, no translucent box |
| One tool | 5 | 4–5 slides |
| Three steps | 3 | 6 slides |

**Proposed slot plan.** Topics come after Research; the slots below fix the tests so they're spread fairly.

| Post | Evening | Group | QR route | Tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| b4p1 | 1 · 7:00 | Fallacy | `?focus=` | **Cream text-only slide 1** |
| b4p2 | 1 · 8:15 | One tool | assessment | Comment prompt |
| b4p3 | 2 · 7:00 | Three steps | `?focus=` | "Keep reading" line |
| b4p4 | 2 · 8:15 | Fallacy | assessment | Comment prompt |
| b4p5 | 3 · 7:00 | One tool | `?focus=` | **Cream text-only slide 1** |
| b4p6 | 3 · 8:15 | One tool | assessment | **Problem + solution hook** |
| b4p7 | 4 · 7:00 | Fallacy | `?focus=` | Comment prompt |
| b4p8 | 4 · 8:15 | Three steps | assessment | No "keep reading" (control) |
| b4p9 | 5 · 7:00 | One tool (**bedtime**) | `?focus=sleep` | Comment prompt |
| b4p10 | 5 · 8:15 | Fallacy | assessment | **Problem + solution hook** |
| b4p11 | 6 · 7:00 | Three steps | `?focus=` | "Keep reading" line + comment prompt |
| b4p12 | 6 · 8:15 | One tool | assessment | Comment prompt |

- **Cream** goes only on first-of-evening posts (clean timing), compared with dark first-of-evening posts.
- **Comment prompts:** 6 with, 6 without, each a one-word question about HER child's preference, tied to the tool.
- **The samples are tiny** (2 vs 2, 2 vs 1). These tests point a direction; they don't prove it.

### Topics
- **At least 8 of 12** have people reacting with lines in the scene (relatives, guests, the teacher, staff, strangers), or a universal or strange-but-common moment.
- **Emotions and outbursts lead:** about 5 of 12, routed to `?focus=emotions` where odd.
- **1 bedtime post.**
- **A few legacy topics with a genuinely new moment or tool,** the rest new. No repeats of B1–B3 topics.

**Starting pool for Research to test (English; not hooks):**
- **Emotions:** his cousin takes the sweet he wanted from the tray at an عزيمة · a relative hands him a toy (unwrapped, or in a bag) and he says «ما أبغاه» · the teacher says "an angel today" and he explodes in the car (legacy L12, new tool) · he hits a cousin over a toy at grandma's while the aunt watches · floor drop in the toy aisle with strangers (L18 family, new place)
- **Strange but common:** presses every lift button with strangers inside · lines up every guest's shoes at the door at an عزيمة
- **Public or seasonal:** won't get out of the car at a كشتة with relatives · bolts in the mall car park (danger, L04/L09 family) · only white rice at the عزيمة buffet while the aunts comment (food)
- **Relatives' advice:** unwanted advice at a family gathering, plus her calm replies (the L25 re-test, new lines) · grandma hands him the biscuit you just said no to
- **Bedtime (1):** staying over at grandma's and he won't sleep while everyone's still up

### CTA (`cta_method.md`)
- Name the outcome she desperately wants in this situation, with certainty («يمكن», «جربي», «لو حابة» are banned), and never as homework («عبي التقييم» is banned).
- The assessment is the bridge, never the promise (claims limited to `assessment_truth.md`).
- Test every CTA: would she click without knowing what's behind it?
- **Match the CTA to the QR route.** Odd posts go to the Living Plan page for that situation, so their CTA must not say "assessment". Even posts can name it as the vehicle («امسحي الكود أو الرابط في البايو»).

### QR and tracking
- One code per post, made with `make_qr.py`, tagged `src=qr&post=b4pN`. The bio link stays `?src=bio`.
- **After each evening:** log day 1 in Post Performance, then read Visits and Submissions by `post`.

### Visual (for Creative Production later)
- Copy is the star, and the slide-1 image supports it.
- Quiet motifs or colour on later slides.
- A fresh look against B3's single teal style, plus a distinct look for the fallacy series.
- The cream text-only slide-1 test (2 posts).

### Rules that bend for labelled tests (please confirm)
1. **Problem + solution hook (b4p6, b4p10)** breaks the B2 rule "one question, no second half". It's suspended for those two posts only.
2. **Cream slide 1 (b4p1, b4p5)** breaks the B3 rule "slide 1 always dark". It's suspended for those two only.
3. **The fallacy label names the assumption of the room (relatives, "people"), never hers,** so the series never blames her. L01's «إن المشكلة عناد» is the model.

### Questions before Research
1. **Confirm:** 12 posts, the 4 / 5 / 3 split and the slot plan above, starting which evening?
2. **The three `src=bio` visits on Nov 24 at 6:18 PM:** your test? And can you run the abandoned-start test so we know drop-offs are logged?
3. **Your full Arabic voice files** ("Arabic Language & Voice System", "Addendum 2") aren't in the repo. Can you share them before Copy (step 7)? Until then the handbook and Feedback & Lessons are the authority.

## Step 1 confirmed (Nov 24)
These are taken as agreed: 12 posts with the 4 / 5 / 3 split and the slot plan; the two hook and two cream rule suspensions (labelled tests only); the «الافتراض» label always naming the room's assumption, never hers; and odd posts' CTAs never mentioning the assessment.

**Still open, asked again before they matter:**
- the start evening (needed at handoff)
- the three `src=bio` visits and the abandoned-start test (needed before the first evening)
- your Arabic voice files (needed before step 7)

## The Batch 4 scorecard (reweighted, total 100)
| # | Item | B3 | **B4** | Why it moved |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Scroll-stop | 18 | **18** | Slide 1 still decides everything. Most viewers never pass slide 2–3. |
| 2 | Recognition: **people reacting + her cost** | 15 | **14** | Now judged on the two reach drivers: lines from the people in the scene (or a universal or strange-but-common moment), and the cost landing on her in the first lines. A hook ending on his behaviour scores low. |
| 3 | Emotion, not apathy | 15 | **13** | Still the core; partly carried by #2 and #4 now. |
| 4 | **Her legacy voice** (was "Her own words") | 12 | **14** | The single biggest gap between legacy (median 3.7K) and us (~500). Scored on short beats, «…» pauses, the stamp → «وأنتي؟» → «وفجأة» rhythm, 2–4 real quoted lines, ONE comic image on her, one love line. |
| 5 | **Value by slide 3** (was "One job") | 10 | **10** | There's no job split any more. Is the named tool on slide 3, shown working, and could she use it tonight? |
| 6 | Trust & safety | 10 | **10** | **Gate.** Never blames her, no diagnosis, no cause, no promise, no therapy, nothing acted out about the child. |
| 7 | Arabic naturalness | 8 | **6** | Still checked line by line by the Arabic Voice Editor; partly overlaps #4. |
| 8 | **The twist** (was "The turn") | 6 | **5** | An unexpected confession that makes her laugh at herself (the coffee-shop model), not a reframe. |
| 9 | Next step (CTA) | 4 | **5** | Custom CTA: the outcome she wants, said with certainty, matched to the post's QR route, and it passes the "would she click without knowing what it is?" test. |
| 10 | Shareable | 2 | **5** | Shares were the breakout marker in legacy (1,598 and 1,106 on the two biggest posts). Would she send it to her sister? |

**How it's used:** the Hook Specialist uses #1–#4 to filter hooks; the Test Panel scores every post on all ten at step 8. **The score is a flag, not proof.** A post that reads aloud like you beats a higher number.

## The agency plan
| Step | Who | What they deliver for B4 |
|---|---|---|
| 3 · Research | **Audience Researcher** and **Market Analyst**, in parallel | **Researcher:** what Saudi and Gulf mothers actually say in the 13 candidate moments, especially **the lines relatives, guests and strangers say to them**, plus her inner voice, as a quote bank (Arabic + gloss, no invented quotes). It ranks the candidates by how universal they are and how much people react in them. **Analyst:** what's wallpaper in this niche now (calm-down tips, "be patient", emotion charts) and the open lane for the «الافتراض» series and for trick-like tools. |
| 4 · Hooks | Hook Specialist | Angles and 4–6 hooks per angle in **your legacy voice**, covering the 12 slots, including the 2 problem + solution hooks and the 4 «الافتراض» openings. Each hook is scored against #1–#4 and tagged with its slot and QR route. |
| 5 · Concepts | Strategist | One concept per slot, plus spares: the named tool, the deepen beat, the proof (method), the twist and the comment question. You pick. |
| 6 · Format | You | Static or video per concept. The default proposal is static, since the slot plan is built for carousels. |
| 7 · Copy | Copywriter | Every post in Arabic, written after reading all 25 Legacy Posts and your voice files. Delivered as a .txt file you can edit (Part M4). |
| 8 · Edit + test | Arabic Voice Editor, then the Test Panel | Native-voice edit; three sceptical mothers react to each post; scored with this card. |
| 9 · Handoff | Strategist | Final posts, captions, a QR code per post (`make_qr.py`), the posting order, and the Airtable rows. |
| After each evening | Analyst | Logs day 1 in Post Performance and reads Visits and Submissions by `post` tag. |

Visual production (the fresh look, the cream test, the «الافتراض» series look) runs afterwards in the Creative Production skill.

steps.report:
## Director's synthesis: both reports in
Full reports are below this summary and in `app/b4/research_audience_b4.md` and `app/b4/research_market_b4.md`.

### Anhar's adjustments (Nov 24)
- **p2:** birthdays aren't celebrated here, so the candles moment is gone. Replaced by the sweets tray at an عزيمة, with another emotions moment and people watching. The alternate is the cousin taking "his" spot next to grandma.
- **p6:** the gift is handed over as it is, or in a bag. No wrapping, no birthday or Christmas feel.
- **p10:** a regular family gathering. No "winter" and no season.
- **Saved as rules in Feedback & Lessons:** check every moment against Saudi daily life (no birthday parties, unwrapped gifts), and no seasonal framing unless there's a real season or occasion now.

### The headline
**The two reports land on the same lane from two directions.**
- The Audience Researcher found that the spark in every moment is **a line someone else says**: the teacher's "angel", the cousin's mum's "kids will be kids", grandma's "don't tell your mum".
- The Market Analyst found that **nobody debunks the social rules of the gathering**. Everyone debunks labels for the child ("stubborn", "attention-seeking"), and that is Stage 5 wallpaper in English.
- So the «الافتراض» series should name **the room's rule**, in a relative's mouth, never a theory about him or a belief of hers. Then a **ten-second tool that works in the room, in front of the witnesses**, and the laugh lands on her.

### What to stay away from (the Analyst's wallpaper list, condensed)
- **Overused calm-down lines:** «حافظي على هدوئك» (stay calm), «نظرات الناس لا تهم» (people's looks don't matter), "every child is different".
- **Overused reframes:** "not giving you a hard time, having a hard time", "connection-seeking", "tantrum vs meltdown" (also clinical for us), "name it to tame it", calm-down corners, emotion charts.
- **Overused relatives advice:** «اشكريها وتجاهلي» (thank her and ignore it), «وحّدي القواعد» (make the rules the same in both houses), the stock reply "this works for us".
- **The diagnosis trap:** every Arabic result on lining things up and picky eating ends in "is it a sign of…" or «استشيري طبيب» (see a doctor). We must never sound like that.
- **Tiredness signal:** there's a backlash against gentle parenting, while a trick like "Jessica" got 11M+ views. Mothers are tired of explanations and still want tricks.

### Proposed slate: research mapped to your 12 slots
| Post | Group · test | Moment | Witness line (the spark) | QR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| b4p1 | Fallacy · cream s1 | Teacher: "an angel today", then he explodes in the car | «ما شاء الله كان ملاك» | emotions |
| b4p2 | One tool · comment | **(replaced)** At an عزيمة, the host passes the sweets tray, his cousin takes the one he wanted, and he falls apart. *Alternate: his cousin sits in "his" spot next to grandma.* | The host: «خذ غيرها حبيبي», the cousin's mum: «عادي… بزران» | assessment |
| b4p3 | Three steps · "keep reading" | Floor drop in the toy aisle, strangers watching. **Twist:** the viral Saudi mother who lay on the floor beside him | "Get control of your child" / staring | emotions |
| b4p4 | Fallacy · comment | Grandma hands him the biscuit you just said no to | «عطوه اللي يبي وبيسكت» | assessment |
| b4p5 | One tool · cream s1 | Lift: someone else presses the button first, and he falls apart with strangers inside | Strangers in a tiny box, six floors | outings |
| b4p6 | One tool · problem + solution hook | **(adjusted)** A relative hands him a toy as it is, or in a bag (never wrapped), and in front of her he says «ما أبغاه» | The aunt: "rude" | assessment |
| b4p7 | Fallacy · comment | «سلّم على خالتك»: he refuses to greet or kiss at the door | «لازم يسلّم على الكل ويبوس راس جدته» | outings |
| b4p8 | Three steps · control | He hits a cousin over a toy at grandma's, the aunt watching | The aunt's silence, then her line | assessment |
| b4p9 | One tool · bedtime · comment | Staying over at grandma's: he won't sleep while everyone's still up | "Leave him, he's not sleepy" | sleep |
| b4p10 | Fallacy · problem + solution hook | **(adjusted)** Unwanted advice at a regular family gathering (no season) | «خلوه عندي يوم… كلمة وحدة مني ويسكت» | assessment |
| b4p11 | Three steps · "keep reading" + comment | Only white rice at the عزيمة buffet, aunts commenting | The aunts' running commentary | food |
| b4p12 | One tool · comment | He lines up every guest's shoes at the door (strange but common) | The guests' reaction only, never "a sign" | assessment |

- **Coverage:**
  - 5 posts are emotions and outbursts (p1, p2, p3, p6, p8).
  - All 12 have people reacting in the scene.
  - 1 post is bedtime.
  - Legacy topics come back with a new moment or tool: the teacher's angel is L12, the floor drop is L18's family, the relatives are L02/L10.
  - Nothing repeats a Batch 1–3 topic.
- **The fallacy four** are the Analyst's top picks: «كان ملاك», «عطوه وبيسكت», «لازم يسلّم», «خلوه عندي يوم». Each one is the room's rule, never hers. «دلّعتيه» (you've spoiled him) and «قدام الناس يسويها عشان يحرجك» (he does it in front of people to embarrass you) are alternates.
- **Held back:** the كشتة (no evidence, and seasonal) and the car park. Nobody in the car-park scene has a line, which is the type of post that stalled 4 of 4 in Batch 3.

### Two cautions
1. **The shoes (p12)** is the one moment search links to diagnosis. It's safe only if the whole post stays on the guests' reaction and her day. If you'd rather not risk it, the reserve is «دلّعتيه» as a fifth relatives' post.
2. **"Noticing" doesn't go on the tool slide.** The Analyst suggested one "notice whether…" beat on the tool slide, but your Batch 3 rule says noticing lives only in the proof/explainer and the CTA. I'm keeping your rule: the proof slide carries the method line.

### Proof-slide method line (safe, for the Copywriter)
«الخطة الحية: خطة للبيت تنبني من ملاحظاتك أنتي، موقف واحد في كل مرة، وتتعدل حسب استجابة طفلك.»
("The Living Plan: a home plan built from your own observations, one situation at a time, adjusted to how your child responds.") This is only for even posts, or worded without "assessment" on odd ones. It never claims "his whole day", "every two weeks", the reason why, or results.

### The evidence gap (please read)
- **Real Saudi witness lines from the wild are thin.** Search doesn't index TikTok, Snap or X comments.
- **Every forum page we tried to open was blocked** by this session's network: alyaum.com, slaati.com, alukah.net, reddit.com and mumsnet.com.
- So most quotes are English, or your own legacy lines, and every entry is tagged.
- **The best fix is yours:** the comment sections on your legacy breakouts (grandma's 203K, restaurant 39.5K, wall post with 75 comments) are the best source of real Saudi witness lines. If you paste 20–30 comments, or screenshots, before step 7, the Copywriter writes from them.
- I can also ask to open those five sites for a second research pass if you want it.

---

# Audience Researcher
# Audience Research · Batch 4, step 3

## 3. Brief notes

**Real moments, not categories.**
- The line that starts it is spoken by someone else: the teacher's "angel", the cousin's "kids will be kids", grandma's "don't tell your mum".
- The witnesses at a Gulf gathering are a chorus: aunts, grandma, the giver, the host. The evil-eye line (#1) shows that guests and praise carry their own pressure.
- A stranger's kind line (#8) is rarer, and stronger as a final beat.

**Frustrations.**
- Her "no" cancelled in front of him (#12, #21, #22).
- Being judged as a mother for his manners (#2, #11, #23).
- The two-faced day: angel for others, storm for her (#3, #24).
- Her own temper, which she confesses only on anonymous consultation sites (#17–#19). That shame is real, so clear it with love lines and never quote it back at her.

**What builds trust.**
- Name the witness's line exactly.
- Let her laugh at herself (#26 is the coffee-shop model).
- Give a tool that works inside the moment.
- Show the moment from the giver's or aunt's side for a second (#31), without siding with them.

**What breaks trust.**
- The stock replies she's already heard ("this works for us", rehearse "thank you", stay calm).
- Picky-eating and lining-up content that ends in «استشيري طبيب» or "is it a sign of…". Every Arabic result for #7 and #10 does this. **We must not.**
- Clinical causes for the restraint collapse (the English articles name diagnoses).
- Blame («دلعتيه»).

**Biggest gap, and next step.** No Saudi witness lines were found in the wild. The best source is the comment sections on Anhar's legacy breakouts (grandma's 203K, restaurant 39.5K, wall post with 75 comments). Harvest those before step 7. Allowing alyaum.com, slaati.com, alukah.net, reddit.com and mumsnet.com in the network settings would let the next researcher read full threads.

# Market Analyst
# Market research, Batch 4 (step 3): emotions, outbursts, relatives, "it's not stubbornness"

*Method: marketing-sophistication (map, then stage, then gap, then match-check). This builds on `app/research_market.md`, which already found tantrums at Stage 5 and named the Arabic wallpaper («احتوي مشاعره», «سمّي مشاعره», «اصبري»). This file adds what's new for B4. **Evidence gap:** web search doesn't index TikTok or Instagram captions. The Arabic evidence comes from the articles those accounts recycle (Sayidaty, Asharq Al-Awsat, Sabq, Altibbi, Al Jazeera, Eremnews). The English evidence comes from the sources Arabic creators translate (Dr. Becky, Big Little Feelings, Mother.ly, Child Mind). I found no Saudi-dialect creator who clearly owns these topics. That matches the B1 finding, but it's still "observed", not proven.*

## 1. Sophistication stage, with evidence

| Topic | English market | Arabic market | Her heart |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tantrums and outbursts in public or at gatherings | **Stage 5** | **Stage 4** | Stage 5 |
| "It's not stubbornness / not bad behaviour, it's…" | **Stage 4–5** | **Stage 3** | Stage 5 |
| Relatives' unwanted advice | Stage 3 | **Stage 2** (articles only) | Stage 5 |
| Calming tips and emotion regulation | Stage 5 | Stage 4 | Stage 5 |

**Wallpaper (don't lead with any of these):**
- **"Be patient / stay calm first."** «حافظي على هدوئك» appears in every article (Okaz, Sabq, Maspero). «نظرات الناس لا تهم» is the actual Asharq Al-Awsat headline ("people's looks don't matter").
- **"Every child is different"** and "it's a normal stage." Altibbi calls stubbornness a normal bid for independence. (Our «طبيعي» ban already keeps us out of this.)
- **"He's not giving you a hard time, he's having a hard time."** This is Dr. Becky's line, repeated by Mother.ly, Psychology Today, Today's Parent and a dozen blogs. It's the master template of the "it's not X, it's Y" reframe.
- **"Not attention-seeking, connection-seeking."** NBC Think, Nurtured First, Evolutionary Parenting. Also wallpaper: "ignoring tantrums doesn't work" (Mother.ly).
- **"Tantrum vs meltdown."** This is the sensory explanation (Child Mind, Psychology Today, The Mighty, OT Toolbox). It's saturated in English, and it's **off-limits for us anyway** (it's clinical and implies a diagnosis).
- **"Name it to tame it" / "name the emotion."** Already contested inside the field: Dr. Becky says stop naming feelings mid-meltdown, and Hand in Hand says naming can make it worse. Contested wallpaper is the worst kind to lead with.
- **Calm-down corners and emotion charts.** The Bump, WebMD, Mother.ly and Generation Mindful all add the same caveat ("introduce it when calm, not as punishment").
- **"Connection before correction"** and "validate, then set limits" (the CDC's emotion coaching).
- **For relatives:** «اشكريها وتجاهلي النصيحة» ("thank her and ignore the advice") and «وحّدي القواعد بين البيتين» ("make the rules the same in both houses") (Al Jazeera, Sayidaty, e3arabi).

**Exhaustion signal (this is what makes Stage 5).** There is a backlash against gentle parenting: CBC and Romper's "gentle parenting dropouts", and Olivia Owen's 2.6M-view spoof asking her melting-down child for consent to a hug at IKEA. Eremnews has published «كيف جعل تيك توك الآباء يخشون قول لا» ("how TikTok made parents afraid to say no"). The audience is now cynical about *scripts* themselves. In the same feed, the Arabic-covered "Jessica" trick (calling an imaginary person to stop the crying) got 11M+ views. **People are tired of explanations and still hungry for tricks.**

## 2. Our batch's level vs the market's

- **The voice is Stage 5.** Witness scenes, her inner voice, a comic image of her, a love line that clears her. That's identity, and it's what the legacy breakouts did.
- **The tool is Stage 3–4.** One named, trick-like move shown working. Against an Arabic field of advice lists («حضّري مسبقاً، أعطيه خيارات، اهدئي»), that reads as a new mechanism.
- **The proof is Stage 3.** A personalised, evolving home plan built from her observations.
- **Fit: good, with one risk.** The «الافتراض» series uses the exact shape the English market has worn out ("it's not stubbornness, it's…"). In Arabic it's only Stage 3, so it still lands, *as long as* the second half isn't the borrowed one. If «لكن أحياناً…» resolves into sensory overload, "connection-seeking" or "having a hard time", the post joins the wallpaper *and* breaks our rules. **The fix:** the second half names an observable moment ("sometimes the hard part is the leaving, not the shoes"), never a cause inside him, and goes straight to the tool. The tool is the payoff, not the reframe.

## 3. The open lanes

**(a) The «الافتراض» series: the room's rules, not the child's psychology.**
Everyone debunks *labels for the child* (stubborn, manipulative, attention-seeking). **Nobody debunks the social rules of the gathering**: «لازم يسلّم» (he has to greet everyone), «كلمة وحدة مني ويسكت» (one word from me and he'll be quiet), «عطوه وبيسكت» (give it to him and he'll stop), «كان ملاك طول الزيارة» (he was an angel the whole visit). These are Saudi-specific, family-specific, and untranslated from English. How to state them without blaming her or sounding like "not like other advice":
- The label is always in **a relative's mouth, in quotes** («قالت خالته: …»). She's never the one who believes it.
- **Don't argue with the assumption.** Show what it costs *her* in the room (the comic image), then «لكن أحياناً…» plus one observable detail.
- **No meta-claims** («كل النصائح غلط», «عكس اللي يقولونه لك»). The series label does the contrast. Never knock other advice or the relatives themselves. They're family, and the humour stays on her.

**(b) Trick-like tools vs advice.** The Arabic field gives advice for *before* and *after* («حضّري», «بعد ما يهدأ كلميه»). The English field gives *home* tools (corners, charts, scripts). **The open lane is a tool that works in the room, in ten seconds, in front of witnesses**: no corner, no chart, no quiet bedroom. A legacy tool like the wrong shoe is exactly this, and the 11M Jessica trick proves the appetite. Constraint: our tools must be honest moves she makes, not distraction gimmicks promising instant silence. Show "what he does next" in 2–3 beats, never "and it stops".

**(c) Witness scenes with humour on the mother.** The market splits into earnest validation ("you're not a bad mom", "people's looks don't matter") and humour aimed at gentle parents (the IKEA spoof). **Nobody does affectionate humour about her as the referee of the whole majlis**: the aunt's commentary, grandma's counter-ruling, the uncle's «خلوه عندي يوم». The relatives' lines are the chorus. She gets the single comic image («المتحدثة الرسمية باسم الطفل», "the child's official spokeswoman"). The confession twist lands the laugh on her. This is the shape B3's winners (ملكة, جمعة, jacket) and legacy L01 (203K) share.

## 4. The mechanism to lead with (when the room is crowded)

Name it plainly. Don't lead with «خطة مخصصة» ("a customised plan"): sleep consultants and coaching ads have made that wallpaper. Lead with the two parts nobody else claims: **built from what she notices**, and **it changes with him**.

- **Proof-slide wording (safe):** «الخطة الحية: خطة للبيت تنبني من ملاحظاتك أنتي، موقف واحد في كل مرة، وتتعدل حسب استجابة طفلك.» ("The Living Plan: a home plan built from your own observations, one situation at a time, adjusted to how your child responds.")
- **Show it, don't advertise it.** The tool slide can include one *noticing* beat ("notice whether it starts at the door or at the shoes"). That *is* the method in miniature.
- **Don't claim:**
  - "every two weeks" (dropped in B2)
  - "looks at his whole day"
  - "finds the reason / why he does it"
  - "calmer in X days"
  - "proven"
  - testimonials
  - "specialists"
  - six areas
- **Brand "we" is allowed for the method** (Anhar kept «نبدأ بموقف واحد»). Parent "we" stays banned.
- **Odd posts** (on the `?focus=` route) must not say "assessment" on the proof or CTA slide.
- **Emotions CTA:** the outcome is "help him handle hard emotions and recover; calm before it becomes a scene". Name it with certainty, as the goal, not as a promised result.

## 5. Identity angle

**She is the one who knows which minute it turns, and the room doesn't.**
- Every relative in the scene has a theory built from five minutes of watching. She has years of watching.
- The identity line: **"you're the expert in the room, even when you're the only one who isn't talking."** («أنتي أكثر وحدة تعرفه… حتى لو كل المجلس عنده رأي.»)
- It answers stranger checklists and relatives' rulings without attacking either.
- It sets up the mechanism for free: a plan built *from her observations* is the logical next step for the person who already knows him best.
- **Avoid:** "trust your gut" mom-power slogans (English wallpaper), martyr framing, and any label on him.

## 6. Assumption candidates for «الافتراض اللي يصعّب الموضوع»

All of them belong to the room. None is hers. «عناد» (L01) is excluded as already used.

1. **"He does it in front of people on purpose, to embarrass you."**
   - Arabic: «قدام الناس يسويها… عشان يحرجك»
   - Whose: aunts and guests. Topic: anger and outbursts at a gathering.
   - Why open: English answers this with "connection-seeking" jargon, and Arabic doesn't answer it at all. Our answer is observable: "sometimes it's the crowd and the noise of the moment, not a plan." Phrase it without sensory vocabulary, and lead to a room tool.

2. **"Give him what he wants and he'll calm down."**
   - Arabic: «عطوه اللي يبي وبيسكت»
   - Whose: grandma or the uncle (the biscuit you just said no to). Topic: anger and outbursts, relatives.
   - Why open: articles talk about "unifying the rules". Nobody stages the moment the room overrules her mid-outburst, which is very funny on her («قاضية… والحكم انتقض بالاستئناف», "a judge whose ruling just got overturned on appeal").

3. **"One firm word from me and he'll stop."**
   - Arabic: «خلوه عندي يوم… كلمة وحدة مني ويسكت»
   - Whose: the uncle or the father-in-law. Topic: anger and outbursts.
   - Why open: the classic Gulf relative line, untouched online. Strong witness comedy (the uncle tries, the comic image lands on her watching). No blame, because the one who's wrong is the confident outsider.

4. **"He was an angel the whole visit, so it went fine."**
   - Arabic: «ما شاء الله كان ملاك طول الزيارة»
   - Whose: the hosts or the teacher. Topic: emotions (the explosion in the car or at home afterwards; a new tool for L12).
   - Why open: English calls this "restraint collapse", which is clinical jargon and banned for us. Arabic has nothing. Every mother recognises "the car ride home".

5. **"He has to greet everyone and kiss grandma's head."**
   - Arabic: «لازم يسلّم على الكل ويبوس راس جدته»
   - Whose: the family elders. Topic: outings and visits / communication.
   - Why open: purely Saudi and never touched. A refusal to greet reads as «قلة أدب» (rudeness), so it hits her. A tool like "a greeting he chooses" (a wave, a high five) honours the elders without the standoff at the door.

6. **"You've spoiled him."**
   - Arabic: «دلّعتيه… عشان كذا صاير كذا»
   - Whose: the mother-in-law or older relatives. Topic: anger and outbursts.
   - Why open: articles answer it with "explain calmly to grandma". The open move is the legacy love line: «انفجاره معك مو دليل إنك أقل… أحياناً دليل إنك أمانه». It clears her without saying the relative is wrong. **Handle with care:** the line itself blames her, so the post must clear her by slide 2.

7. **"Don't cry, that's shameful… men don't cry."**
   - Arabic: «عيب… الرجال ما يبكون»
   - Whose: relatives (often said kindly). Topic: emotions.
   - Why open: "name the emotion" is English wallpaper, but nobody stages the Gulf «عيب» moment and gives her a ten-second move to use *in front of* the speaker. **Avoid** turning it into a gender lecture.

8. **"He'll grow out of it."**
   - Arabic: «لما يكبر بيعقل… خليه»
   - Whose: everyone, kindly. Topic: any; best fits transitions or outbursts.
   - Why open: nobody argues with it because it's comforting. Our angle isn't "it's wrong". It's "waiting is a plan with no first step", which is a natural bridge to "one situation at a time".
   - **No promise** that acting now changes anything.

**Recommended four (emotions lead):** #3 «كلمة وحدة مني», #4 «كان ملاك», #2 «عطوه وبيسكت», #5 «لازم يسلّم». Keep #1 and #6 as one-tool alternates.
